connection_sequence.description: Passive (normal): scan -> match sps/tps + fff0 + 9-byte manufacturer data -> decode. No connection ever required. Optional poll: connect -> service fff0 -> read fff2 (temp/hum) -> disconnect. Battery comes from the advertisement byte 7 only.

manufacturer_data.description: Deliberately NO company_id filter: the temperature occupies the company-ID position of the manufacturer data, so the reported id changes with every reading. Identify by local name "sps"/"tps" + fff0 service UUID + 9-byte manufacturer data.

device.name: Inkbird IBS-TH1 / IBS-TH2 Thermometer-Hygrometer
device.notes:
Battery-powered BLE temperature/humidity sensors (IBS-TH1, IBS-TH2, and the IBS-P01B pool thermometer variant) that broadcast readings in BLE advertisement manufacturer data — no connection required for live values. Official app: com.inkbird.inkbirdapp ("Inkbird").
Sources (no APK teardown was needed or used for this spec): the Bluetooth-Devices/inkbird-ble parser library (backs the Home Assistant core inkbird integration), which is itself copied from Ernst79's bleparser (the ble_monitor custom component), plus the library's test suite which pins the byte layout against captured advertisements. Confidence: parser-library-derived, corroborated by raw advertisement captures in the test suite; not re-verified against hardware here.
ADVERTISEMENT QUIRK — there is NO company ID. The manufacturer-specific AD structure (type 0xFF) is 9 bytes and the temperature occupies the two bytes where the Bluetooth company identifier would normally sit. Stacks therefore report the temperature as the "company id" (e.g. a reading of 20.44 °C surfaces as manufacturer_data key 2044 = 0x07FC). Two consequences: (1) discovery must NOT key on a fixed company id — every distinct reading appears as a distinct manufacturer-data entry, and consecutive readings can show up as multiple changed entries; (2) match on local name ("sps" / "tps") plus advertised service UUID 0000fff0 plus the 9-byte total length instead.
ON-AIR MANUFACTURER DATA (9 bytes, offsets from the start of the AD structure content, i.e. including the pseudo company-ID bytes):
  bytes 0-1: temperature, signed int16 LE, /100.0 °C
             (proven: capture fc 07 c7 12 00 c8 3d 56 06 ->
             0x07FC = 2044 -> 20.44 °C, inkbird-ble test_sps)
  bytes 2-3: humidity, uint16 LE, /100.0 %  (0x12C7 = 4807 -> 48.07 %)
  bytes 4-6: unidentified, varies between captures
  byte 7:    battery percent 0-100  (0x56 = 86)
  byte 8:    flags/packet variant (0x06 / 0x08 observed), unknown
IBS-TH2/P01B ("tps") uses the same 9-byte layout; humidity reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor and the parser only reports it when non-zero. Readings with humidity > 100 % are corrupt packets and should be dropped whole (inkbird-ble issue #141).
CONNECTED MODE (optional): the same reading can be polled over GATT. Service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, characteristic 0000fff2-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (read): temperature int16 LE /100 at bytes 0-1, humidity uint16 LE /100 at bytes 2-3 — i.e. the advertisement layout WITHOUT the pseudo-company-id interpretation and without the battery byte (battery is advertisement-only). No pairing, bonding or authentication. The advertisement already carries every field, so polling is only useful as a freshness fallback.
FAMILY CROSS-REFERENCE: Inkbird ships several incompatible protocols under similar names, and 0000fff0 is shared between them:
  - This spec: IBS-TH1/TH2/P01B sensors, names "sps"/"tps", 9-byte ads.
  - iBBQ-1/2/4/6 BBQ thermometers also advertise the fff0 service but
    with names containing "iBBQ"/"xBBQ" and 12/14/18/22-byte
    manufacturer data (probe temps at the tail) — see the sibling spec
    ibbq-meat-thermo (0xfff0 binary GATT protocol, app com.inkbird.ibbtgo).
  - IBT-2X/IBT-4XS/IBBQ-4BW use the 0000ff00 ASCII-hex command protocol
    — see the sibling spec inkbird-bbq-thermometer.
Discriminate by local name + manufacturer-data length + service UUID, never by service UUID alone.

credentials.notes: BLE advertisement broadcast, no auth. No Wi-Fi on this model family.

factory_reset.effect: No factory reset exists or is needed: the device holds no credentials, bindings or client state. Removing the battery for 10+ seconds is the only reset relevant to a BLE client — the device simply resumes broadcasting.

methods.description: Passive scan: match local name "sps"/"tps" and the fff0 service UUID, take the 9-byte manufacturer data, decode temperature, humidity and battery. Optionally connect and read 0000fff2 for a fresh sample.

steps.action: Insert the battery; the sensor starts advertising immediately.
Scan for name sps/tps with service UUID 0000fff0 and a 9-byte manufacturer-data AD structure.
Decode temperature (bytes 0-1, s16 LE, /100), humidity (bytes 2-3, u16 LE, /100), battery (byte 7).
steps.expect: Live readings with every advertisement; humidity above 100% marks a corrupt packet — drop it.

setup.notes: No provisioning, pairing, bonding or account. The device advertises as soon as a battery is fitted; readings are decoded passively. Confidence high: the decode is pinned by captured advertisements in the inkbird-ble test suite and runs in production in the Home Assistant core inkbird integration.

rejoin.notes: Broadcast-only with no bond: any number of clients can decode the advertisements, and switching controllers is just scanning from the new one.

variants.notes: Temperature + humidity + battery in the 9-byte advertisement.
Same 9-byte format. Humidity field reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor (the P01B pool thermometer); report humidity only when non-zero (inkbird-ble behaviour).

entities.name: Humidity
entities.notes: IBS-TH1 only; IBS-TH2/P01B reports 0 when no humidity sensor is fitted — suppress zero.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Advertisement byte 7 only; not present in the GATT poll.

IBS_TH_Advertisement.description: 9-byte manufacturer-specific AD structure (type 0xFF). Byte 0 is the start of the AD content — the pseudo company-ID position that actually carries the temperature.

fields.description: Bytes 0-1, signed int16 LE, /100.0 °C. Surfaces to BLE stacks as the manufacturer-data company id.
fields.name: temperature

fields.description: Bytes 2-3, uint16 LE, /100.0 % RH. Drop the packet if decoded humidity exceeds 100% (corrupt).
fields.name: humidity

parse_rules: Do not match or filter on the company-ID position; it is data.

format.name: humidity
format.notes: Reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor (IBS-TH2/P01B); report only when non-zero.

characteristics.name: sensor_data
characteristics.notes: Current reading, same field layout as the advertisement head: temperature int16 LE /100 °C at bytes 0-1, humidity uint16 LE /100 % at bytes 2-3. No battery byte here — battery is only in the advertisement.

services.name: Inkbird Sensor Service
services.notes: Shared with the iBBQ BBQ-thermometer family — do not treat the service UUID alone as identification. Connected access is optional; the advertisement carries every field.
